mainTopic: The priestly gifts: why קדשים are exempt from זרוע, לחיים and קבה, why חולין are exempt from חזה ושוק, and the status of blemished קדשים
overview: This amud opens the chapter on the priestly gifts. The משנה rules that the זרוע, לחיים and קבה apply everywhere and at all times, but only to חולין, not to קדשים. A קל וחומר would have obligated קדשים too, but the פסוק 'ואתן אותם' limits the כהן's share of a sacrifice to the חזה ושוק. The משנה then contrasts two kinds of blemished קדשים. If the מום came before the הקדש, the redeemed animal is like חולין and owes the gifts. If the הקדש came first, much of its holiness stays. In the גמרא, it asks why the פסוק was needed when the קל וחומר seems easy to refute. After trying several bases, it shows that the קל וחומר from a bought or orphaned animal really works. It then asks the reverse: why don't חולין owe חזה ושוק? The answer is the word 'וזה' in the פסוק. The amud ends by questioning whether waving חולין was ever possible, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The priestly gifts apply everywhere, but only to non-sacred animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the gifts of זרוע, לחיים and קבה apply in ארץ ישראל and outside it, with or without the בית המקדש, to חולין but not to מוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The foreleg, the jaw and the maw must be given to the כהן in ארץ ישראל and outside it, whether or not the בית המקדש stands. This applies to ordinary animals, not to sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the basic rule: when does the מצוה of giving the זרוע, לחיים and קבה to a כהן apply?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה has no limit of place or time. It is not tied to ארץ ישראל and not tied to the בית המקדש. The one limit the משנה gives is the kind of animal: only חולין are included, and מוקדשין are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the opening of the משנה text
The foreleg (shoulder) of the animal, given to the כהן
The jaw (cheeks), given to the כהן
The maw (stomach), given to the כהן
Ordinary, non-sacred animals
Animals consecrated as sacrifices

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not in the presence of the בית' does not mean the מצוה is weaker. It means the מצוה applies in full even when there is no בית המקדש, unlike many other priestly gifts.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The foreleg, the jaw, and the maw
apply in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael,
in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple,
phrases.notes: He means: both when the בית המקדש is standing and when it is not.

phrases.english: to non-sacred animals, but not to sacrificial animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזְּרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה נוֹהֲגִין בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gifts of זרוע, לחיים and קבה apply in all places and times, to חולין only and not to מוקדשין.

steps.title: A logical argument that sacrifices should owe the gifts too
steps.stepSummary: The משנה raises a קל וחומר: if חולין, which owe no חזה ושוק, still owe the gifts, then קדשים, which do owe חזה ושוק, should surely owe the gifts as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: ordinary animals don't have to give the breast and thigh, yet they must give the gifts. Sacrifices do have to give the breast and thigh, so surely they must give the gifts too!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains why it had to say 'not to מוקדשין'. It sets up a logical argument that would have included them, so the next step can knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument says קדשים carry a stronger priestly obligation (חזה ושוק) than חולין do. If the weaker case, חולין, owes the gifts, the stronger case should owe them all the more. This argument challenges the ruling of step 1 that excludes מוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It would have been logical'; opens a reasoned argument
An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
The breast and thigh of a שלמים offering, given to the כהן
The priestly gifts: זרוע, לחיים and קבה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. It is a 'you might think' argument that the משנה brings only so that it can reject it.

phrases.english: For by right it should be:
If non-sacred animals,
which are not obligated in breast and thigh,
are obligated in the gifts,
then sacrificial animals, which are obligated in breast and thigh,
is it not right that they are obligated in the gifts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exclusion of מוקדשין using logic
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the gifts do not apply to מוקדשין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: קדשים carry a stronger priestly obligation (חזה ושוק) than חולין, so they should owe the gifts as well.

steps.title: A verse limits the priest to breast and thigh from sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ואתן אותם לאהרן הכהן ולבניו לחק עולם' teaches that from קדשים the כהן receives only what that passage mentions, the חזה ושוק, and not the other gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says, 'I have given them to אהרן the כהן and his sons as a due forever.' This teaches that from sacrifices the כהן gets only what is mentioned there.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the קל וחומר with a פסוק. The Torah itself limits what the כהן takes from sacrifices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse speaks about the חזה ושוק of שלמים. Reading 'them' as limiting, the כהן's share of קדשים is fixed at what is listed there. A clear פסוק overrides a logical argument, so the exclusion of מוקדשין from step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse states'; brings a פסוק to settle a question
As a fixed, permanent portion
He has only; a limiting reading
In this passage or topic

steps.whatToRemember: From sacrifices the כהן gets only the חזה ושוק. The זרוע, לחיים and קבה come only from חולין.

phrases.english: Therefore, the verse states:
"And I have given them to Aaron the priest
and to his sons as a due forever"

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן.
phrases.english: he has only that which is stated in the matter.
phrases.notes: What is stated in that verse is the breast and the thigh, so that is all the כהן gets from a sacrifice.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וָאֶתֵּן אֹתָם לְאַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר, קדשים should owe the gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק limits the כהן's share of קדשים to the חזה ושוק, so קדשים are exempt from the gifts.

steps.title: Animals blemished before consecration become ordinary after redemption
steps.stepSummary: קדשים that had a מום קבוע before they were consecrated become like חולין once redeemed. They owe בכורה and the gifts, may be shorn and worked, and their offspring and milk are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an animal already had a permanent blemish when it was consecrated and was later redeemed, it counts as an ordinary animal. Its firstborn is a בכור, it owes the gifts, it may be sheared and used for work, and its young and milk are permitted after redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule about a special kind of קדשים: animals that were blemished before they were consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an animal was never fit for the מזבח, so its sanctity is weaker and goes only on its value. Once redeemed, it fully returns to חולין status. That is why the gifts apply to it, unlike the קדשים excluded in step 1, and why the usual bans on shearing, work, offspring and milk fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
Consecration of an animal to holiness
Redemption, which transfers the holiness to money
The law of the firstborn animal
To be shorn and to be used for work, both forbidden with קדשים
Their offspring and their milk

steps.whatToRemember: The order matters: if the blemish came before the consecration, the redeemed animal is treated as fully ordinary, gifts included.
steps.confusionAlert: This rule does not contradict step 1. Step 1 excludes real קדשים. This step is about animals whose holiness was weaker from the start and is gone after redemption.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exemption from the gifts depends on the animal's actual holy status, not on whether it was ever called קדשים.

phrases.english: All sacrificial animals
in which a permanent blemish preceded their consecration,
and they were redeemed,
are obligated in the firstborn law and in the gifts,
phrases.notes: The firstborn law here applies to the animal's offspring.

phrases.english: and they go out to non-sacred status with regard to being shorn and being worked,
and their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁקָּדַם מוּם קָבוּעַ לְהֶקְדֵּשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case of קדשים that, once redeemed, are treated like חולין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redeemed animals whose permanent blemish came before their consecration owe בכורה and the gifts, may be shorn and worked, and their offspring and milk are permitted.

steps.title: More rules for animals whose blemish came before their consecration
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the case from step 4. These animals carry no penalty for being slaughtered outside the Temple and cannot create a תמורה. If they die before being redeemed, they can still be redeemed. All of this applies except to a בכור or מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who slaughters these animals outside the Temple is exempt. They do not make a substitute animal holy. If they die, they may be redeemed. This is true of all of them except the firstborn and the tithe animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing the ways an animal that had a מום קבוע before its הקדש is treated more leniently than ordinary קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the blemish came first, the animal's holiness was weak from the start. So the serious penalties of קדשים fall away: no כרת for slaughtering outside, and no power to make a תמורה. בכור and מעשר are different because their holiness comes on its own, not through a person's הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the Temple courtyard
An animal swapped for a holy animal, which becomes holy too
They are redeemed (bought out of their holiness)
A firstborn male animal
The tithe animal (every tenth animal)

phrases.english: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means outside the Temple courtyard, and 'exempt' means from the punishment of כרת.

phrases.english: and they do not make a substitute holy,
and if they died, they may be redeemed,
except for the firstborn and the tithe animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of leniencies from step 4 and adds the exception of בכור and מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the מום came before the הקדש, the animal has no קדושת הגוף: even before it is redeemed there is no שחוטי חוץ liability and no תמורה, and if it dies it may be redeemed. בכור and מעשר are the exception.

steps.title: The opposite case: consecration came before the blemish
steps.stepSummary: The משנה turns to animals that were consecrated first and only later got a permanent blemish. After פדיון they are exempt from בכורה and the מתנות, but they may still not be shorn or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take any animal whose consecration came before its blemish, or that had a passing blemish before consecration and only later got a permanent one, and was then redeemed. It is exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts. But it does not become fully non-holy: it still may not be shorn or used for work.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the contrasting case: the animal was holy first and became blemished afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מום עובר (a temporary blemish) does not count as the kind of blemish that weakens the הקדש, so it is treated like 'holy first.' Here the holiness was full when it began. So even after פדיון some holiness remains, and shearing and working the animal stay forbidden. Unlike step 4, these animals are exempt from the מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that goes away
A permanent blemish
Consecration, making an animal holy
To be shorn and to be put to work

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In step 4 the animal was blemished first and owes the מתנות. Here it was holy first and is exempt from the מתנות.

phrases.english: All animals whose consecration came before their blemish,
or that had a temporary blemish before their consecration,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר מִכָּאן נוֹלַד לָהֶם מוּם קָבוּעַ,
phrases.english: and afterward a permanent blemish developed in them,
and they were redeemed:
they are exempt from the firstborn law and from the gifts,
and they do not go out to non-holy status to be shorn and to be worked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the opposite case to steps 4 and 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the הקדש came before the מום קבוע, the redeemed animal is exempt from בכורה and the מתנות, but it may still not be shorn or worked.

steps.title: Strict rules when the הקדש came first
steps.stepSummary: For animals that were holy first, offspring and milk stay forbidden even after פדיון. While the animal is still consecrated, slaughtering it outside brings liability and it can make a תמורה, and if it dies unredeemed it must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption. Someone who slaughters them outside the Temple is liable. They do make a substitute animal holy. If they die, they must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the 'holy first' case by listing the strict rules that still apply. They are the exact opposite of the rules in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every rule here flips a rule from step 5, but they do not all apply at the same time. Only offspring and milk are about after redemption: they stay forbidden when the young was conceived before the פדיון and born after it (Rashi). The other rules describe the animal while it is still consecrated: slaughtering it outside brings liability (Rashi: with a minor eye blemish, which רבי עקיבא says is not taken down once it was brought up on the altar), it makes a תמורה, and if it dies before redemption it is buried rather than redeemed. This shows how much holiness stays when the הקדש came first.

keyTerms.meaning: Their offspring
Their milk
Redemption
They must be buried

steps.whatToRemember: The order matters. מום before הקדש means that after פדיון the animal is almost plain חולין and owes the מתנות. הקדש before מום means it stays partly holy and is exempt from the מתנות.

phrases.english: and their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption,
and one who slaughters them outside is liable,
phrases.notes: Before redemption, while the animal is still consecrated (Rashi).

phrases.english: and they do make a substitute holy,
and if they died, they must be buried.
phrases.notes: An animal that died before it was redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'holy first' case and mirrors the rules of step 5 in reverse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the הקדש came first: offspring and milk stay forbidden even after פדיון; while the animal is still consecrated, slaughtering it outside brings liability and it makes a תמורה; and if it dies before redemption it must be buried.

steps.title: Why would we think sacrificial animals owe the gifts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's use of the word 'אותם'. It points out what that implies: without the פסוק, we would have said that קדשים owe the מתנות. That seems surprising and needs explaining.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason sacrificial animals are exempt is only that the Torah wrote 'them.' So without that word, would I really have said that sacrificial animals owe the gifts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about the משנה's derivation from steps 2 and 3. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה needed a פסוק to stop the קל וחומר, so it must have thought the קל וחומר would otherwise work. The גמרא is surprised, because that קל וחומר looks easy to break, as the next step shows. If logic could not obligate קדשים anyway, why was the פסוק needed?

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is (only) that...
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
But if not for this
I would have thought

phrases.english: Gemara:
The reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'them,'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from step 3: ויקרא 7:34.

phrases.english: but if not for this,
would I have said that sacrificial animals owe the gifts?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא אוֹתָם, הָא לָאו הָכִי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the blemished-animal rules and goes back to the משנה's exclusion of קדשים from the מתנות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption (steps 2 and 3) that, without 'אותם', the קל וחומר would make קדשים owe the מתנות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From the fact that a פסוק was needed, we learn that without it the קל וחומר would have made קדשים owe the מתנות. But that קל וחומר can be refuted (step 9), so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The קל וחומר from ordinary animals breaks down
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר from חולין to קדשים is refuted, because חולין owe בכורה and קדשים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about ordinary animals? They are special because they owe the firstborn obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר that would have made קדשים owe the מתנות. It points out that ordinary animals have an extra obligation that קדשים don't have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said: if lowly חולין owe the מתנות, holy קדשים surely do. But a קל וחומר only works if the 'weaker' case is weaker in every way. חולין are stricter in one area, since they owe בכורה, so maybe that strictness is what makes them owe the מתנות.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute; the argument can be broken
"What about X? It is special because...": the standard way to break a קל וחומר
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
The priestly gifts from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the jaw and the stomach
The holiness of a firstborn animal, which is given to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging the halacha that קדשים are exempt. It is asking why the משנה needed a פסוק to exempt them: if this קל וחומר breaks down anyway, the exemption would follow without a פסוק. Steps 10 to 14 try to rescue the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: There is room to refute this:
phrases.notes: He means the קל וחומר from חולין that lay behind the surprise in step 8.

phrases.english: What about ordinary animals?
They are special because they are obligated in the firstborn law!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְחוּלִּין שֶׁכֵּן חַיָּיבִין בִּבְכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר that explained why, without the פסוק, we would think קדשים owe the מתנות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from ordinary חולין to קדשים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חולין have a stringency of their own (בכורה) that קדשים lack, so they are not weaker in every way.

steps.title: Trying to learn from male animals, which is also rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to build the קל וחומר from male animals, which don't owe בכורה, but males owe ראשית הגז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from male animals. But what about males? They are special because they owe the first shearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new starting point for the קל וחומר: male animals. It then immediately rejects that as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Males have no בכורה problem, since they never give birth, and yet they owe the מתנות. That would seem to avoid the earlier refutation. But male sheep owe ראשית הגז, an obligation קדשים don't have, so the קל וחומר breaks again.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come, meaning let us derive it from
Male animals
The first shearing of wool, which is given to the כהן

phrases.english: Let it be derived from male animals –
phrases.notes: Males never give birth, so the בכורה obligation can't apply to them.

phrases.english: What about males?
They are special because they are obligated in the first shearing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new base for the קל וחומר that avoids the בכורה refutation, then refutes it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר built from male animals.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Males owe ראשית הגז, a stringency קדשים lack.

steps.title: Trying to learn from male goats, which is also rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries male goats, which owe neither בכורה nor ראשית הגז, but goats enter the pen for tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from male goats. But what about male goats? They are special because they enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries male goats as the base, since they avoid both earlier problems. Then it rejects this too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Male goats never give birth, and goat hair is not subject to ראשית הגז, yet they owe the מתנות. But they are part of מעשר בהמה, where animals pass through a pen to be counted. קדשים are not, so the קל וחומר still fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Male goats
The animal pen
To be tithed; this refers to מעשר בהמה, where every tenth animal is counted out

phrases.english: From male goats –
phrases.notes: Read it as 'let it be derived from male goats.' The word תיתי from the line before is understood.

phrases.english: What about male goats?
They are special because they enter the pen to be tithed!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְּיָישִׁים – מָה לִתְיָישִׁים, שֶׁכֵּן נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks a base that avoids both בכורה and ראשית הגז, then refutes it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר built from male goats.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Male goats are subject to מעשר בהמה, which קדשים are not.

steps.title: Trying to learn from old male goats, which is also rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries old male goats, which were already tithed, but even they once entered the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from old male goats. But what about old goats? They are special because they did enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another base, old male goats, whose tithing is already behind them, and rejects this one too. The search is not over: the next step tries a bought or orphaned animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old goats have no obligation left today: no בכורה, no ראשית הגז, and no tithing still ahead. Still, they did go through the tithing pen at one point, and קדשים never do, so this base fails too. The גמרא keeps looking for a base with no such stringency, because it is trying to show that the קל וחומר really works and the פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Old animals, here old male goats
They already entered, in the past

steps.whatToRemember: So far every base for the קל וחומר (חולין, males, male goats, old goats) has had some obligation that קדשים lack. The גמרא keeps searching, because it wants to show that the קל וחומר can work and so the פסוק 'אותם' is really needed (step 14).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the classic way a קל וחומר gets tested. The גמרא keeps swapping in a 'weaker' base, and each time it searches for one stringency that base has and the other case lacks.

phrases.english: From old male goats –
What about old goats?
They are special because they did enter the pen to be tithed!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִזְּקֵנִים – מָה לִזְקֵנִים, שֶׁכֵּן נִכְנְסוּ לְדִיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks a base whose tithing obligation is already over, then refutes it. The search continues in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר built from old male goats.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even old goats were once subject to מעשר בהמה, while קדשים never are.

steps.title: Trying a bought or orphaned animal, which is not tithed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to build the קל וחומר from a לקוח or a יתום, which are never tithed. It is pushed back: animals of their kind do go into the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from a bought animal or an orphaned animal. But what about a bought or orphaned animal? Animals of their kind go into the pen to be tithed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new starting animal for the קל וחומר: a bought animal or an orphaned one, since neither is tithed. Then it pokes a hole in that: other animals of the same kind are tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, old goats failed because they once went into the pen. A לקוח or יתום never goes into the pen at all, so it seems like a better choice. But the objection is that their kind (sheep, goats, cattle) does get tithed, and that link to מעשר is still a special quality קדשים seem to lack.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was bought. It is exempt from animal tithe.
An orphaned animal, born after its mother died. It is also exempt from animal tithe.
The pen the animals are brought into to be counted for tithing.
To be tithed, meaning to go through מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: From a bought animal or an orphaned one
phrases.notes: The גמרא now tries starting the קל וחומר from these two, since neither one is ever tithed.

phrases.english: What is special about a bought or orphaned animal?
That animals of their kind go in
to the pen to be tithed!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְלָקוּחַ וְיָתוֹם, שֶׁכֵּן נִכְנָסִין בְּמִינָן לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next attempt to build the קל וחומר, after old goats failed in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using a לקוח or יתום as the base of the קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their kind (במינן) still enters the pen for tithing, so they have a link to מעשר.

steps.title: The 'their kind' argument works for קדשים too, so the קל וחומר stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if 'their kind' counts, then קדשים also have a kind that is tithed. So the objection falls, the קל וחומר works, and the פסוק 'אותם' is really needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are talking about their kind? Sacrificial animals also have a kind that goes into the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last objection. If we only care about the animal's kind, then קדשים are also of a kind that gets tithed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between the לקוח or יתום and קדשים disappears, because both are linked to tithing only through their kind. So the קל וחומר from a לקוח or יתום holds. This explains why, without the פסוק, we really would have said קדשים owe the מתנות, which answers the question from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Through their kind: other animals of the same species, not the animal itself.
Animals set aside as sacrifices.

steps.whatToRemember: The קל וחומר from a לקוח or יתום really works. So קדשים would owe the מתנות if not for the word 'אותם' in the פסוק, which is why the משנה needs it.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not another failed attempt. Here the גמרא defends the קל וחומר, and that shows the פסוק is truly needed.

phrases.english: You are talking about their kind?
Sacrificial animals too:
animals of their kind go into the pen to be tithed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overturns the objection in step 13, so the קל וחומר holds and the question of step 8 is answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without the פסוק, a קל וחומר from a לקוח or יתום would make קדשים owe the מתנות. So 'אותם' is needed to exempt them.

steps.title: Should ordinary animals give breast and thigh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא runs a reverse קל וחומר. קדשים don't owe the מתנות yet give חזה ושוק, so חולין, which do owe the מתנות, should surely give חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let ordinary animals owe breast and thigh by a קל וחומר: if sacrificial animals, which don't owe the gifts, do owe breast and thigh, then ordinary animals, which do owe the gifts, should surely owe breast and thigh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge in the opposite direction. It asks why ordinary slaughtered animals don't have to give the כהן the חזה ושוק, the way certain קרבנות do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know קדשים are free from the מתנות, the גמרא compares the two kinds of animals. Each has a gift the other lacks. Since חולין have the 'stronger' duty of the מתנות, logic suggests they should also give חזה ושוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast and thigh that are given to the כהן from certain קרבנות, such as a שלמים.
Ordinary animals that are not sacrifices.
The כהן's gifts from an ordinary slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw.
'Is it not logical?' This is how the second half of a קל וחומר is put.

phrases.english: Then let ordinary animals owe the breast and thigh
by an argument from the lighter case to the stricter one:
If sacrificial animals, which don't owe the gifts,
do owe the breast and thigh,
then ordinary animals, which do owe the gifts,
isn't it logical that they owe the breast and thigh?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיִהְיוּ חוּלִּין חַיָּיבִין בְּחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that קדשים are exempt from the מתנות, then turns the comparison around.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted halacha that חולין don't owe חזה ושוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: קדשים, the weaker case for the מתנות, still give חזה ושוק. So חולין, the stronger case, should give it too.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'this': only the listed gifts come from ordinary animals
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וזה יהיה משפט הכהנים' teaches that only 'this', the זרוע, לחיים and קבה, is given from חולין, and nothing else, so חזה ושוק are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And this shall be the priests' due.' 'This' is given, but nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר with a פסוק. The word 'זה' limits the gifts from ordinary animals to the ones listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about ordinary slaughtering lists the foreleg, jaw and maw and calls them 'this'. The word 'this' marks off a closed list, so other gifts like חזה ושוק are left out. A clear פסוק overrides a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The priests' due': the gifts the Torah gives the כהנים.
'This': a word that limits the rule to what is mentioned.
Something else; anything not on the list.

steps.whatToRemember: קדשים are free from the מתנות because of 'אותם', and חולין are free from חזה ושוק because of 'וזה'. Each kind of animal has only its own gifts.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And this shall be the priests' due"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:3. This is the פסוק that lists the foreleg, jaw and maw.

phrases.english: "This": yes,
anything else: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְזֶה יִהְיֶה מִשְׁפַּט הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 with a limiting word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק (מיעוט) overrides the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Logic suggests that חולין should give חזה ושוק, just like קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'זה' limits the gifts from חולין to the foreleg, jaw and maw, so they don't give חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Why would we need a verse? Waving חולין seems impossible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the need for 'זה'. חזה ושוק require תנופה before ה׳, so they could never come from חולין waved outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason חולין are exempt is that the Torah wrote 'this'. So without it, would I really have thought חולין must give חזה ושוק? But these parts need waving. Where would you wave them? If outside the מקדש, that can't be, because it says 'before ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we needed the word 'זה' to exempt חולין, since there seems to be no possible way to wave חולין anyway. It starts a two-sided question (outside or inside), and here it rules out the 'outside' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 implied that without 'זה' we would have obligated חולין in חזה ושוק. But חזה ושוק require תנופה 'before ה׳', which means inside the מקדש. So waving them outside is impossible, and the חיוב seems unworkable even without a פסוק. The 'inside' option still has to be ruled out, and that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
I would have thought (an early assumption before the answer)
Waving: the כהן waves the parts back and forth
Outside (the עזרה, the Temple courtyard)
'Before ה׳': it must be done in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the פסוק 'זה' is wrong. It is asking why the פסוק is needed, if the logic of תנופה already rules out חולין.

phrases.english: But the reason is that the Merciful One wrote "this"
phrases.notes: This is the word 'זה' from the previous step: 'וזה יהיה משפט הכהנים'.

phrases.english: so if not for this,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא חוּלִּין חַיָּיבִין בְּחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק?
phrases.english: would I have said that non-sacred animals are obligated in breast and thigh?
But it requires waving,
so where would one wave them?
If outside the Temple,
it is written "before the Lord"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:30. 'Before ה׳' means it has to happen in the מקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״זֶה״, הָא לָאו הָכִי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16 by asking why the derivation from 'זה' is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'וזה יהיה משפט הכהנים' to exempt חולין from חזה ושוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חזה ושוק require תנופה לפני ה׳. Waving outside the מקדש is impossible because of the פסוק, so the obligation seems unworkable for חולין even without a פסוק. The inside option is addressed next.
